decision: Determine whether a tiny CPU-trained copy-and-vocabulary speculative decoder predicts request-disjoint Gemma 4 c32 continuations better than the existing deterministic in-request n-gram drafter.

claims_allowed: offline exact-token accepted-prefix behavior on the bound synthetic c32 workload
whether this learned mechanism merits a matched target-GPU endpoint integration

hypothesis: A token-identity-invariant copy head plus a small learned vocabulary head can generalize repetitive continuations to unseen token IDs and achieve useful depth-4 exact prefixes without running the target model during training.

controls: corpus n-gram trained only on the 28 training requests
deterministic in-request n-gram using only the current request prefix
measurement.primary_metric: mean accepted draft tokens per verification on four request-disjoint holdout responses

quality_gate: All labels must be reconstructed from the raw cumulative output_ids/token_ids sequence. The target verifier remains the sole output authority in any later integration.
stop_rule: Do not spend GPU budget on endpoint integration unless the trained decoder beats the deterministic in-request n-gram control or provides a materially cheaper implementation at statistically indistinguishable acceptance. Treat a synthetic-workload result only as a pipeline and mechanism result.
timeout: 20 minutes wall time on the controller CPU
